answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a lineage ladder: every agent carries a signed record of completed work, and valuable jobs need a lineage above a threshold. A new identity starts on the flat mesa top, exposed, with nothing to show, and must climb by doing real tasks, each carved like marble into its record. A jade seal from a high-reputation peer can speed the climb, but seals are scarce and issuers lose standing for vouching for a fraud. An attacker wanting a hundred fake agents must pay for a hundred real work histories, turning a cheap identity flood into an expensive labour bill.
